ground_truth_kind.description: How the correct answers this plan grades against were produced: labelled by a person, labelled by another AI/agent, or derived mechanically (e.g. a deterministic oracle or replay). Required when stage is gate; optional otherwise.

subject_identity.description: The identity of the classifier or service actually graded by this plan's results -- its name and the exact version under evaluation (the counterpart, on the spec side, of quoin-measurement's MeasurementCollection subject/tool_version fields on the evidence side). Optional, but recommended on every plan and especially on gate-stage plans, so a pass/fail decision can be traced back to what was actually tested.

preregistration.description: Tamper evidence only, not an ordering proof (PLAT-936). `bar_digest` is a sha256 digest over the normalized text of this document's own "Comparison and Enforcement" section, checked at measurement intake against that section as the document reads at admission time. A mismatch means the section was edited after the digest was recorded, and the collection is refused. This does NOT prove the bar predates any result -- a commit's author-date and a collection's own timestamp are both self-reported strings nobody attests independently, which is why the ordering check originally proposed for this was found unbuildable (PLAT-935). It also does not stop an evaluator reporting only a favourable pre-registered variant, does not stop a repeated re-run until one passes, and does not stop editing an unprotected input such as the baseline instead of the bar text itself. Optional.

bar_digest.description: sha256 of the "Comparison and Enforcement" section's text, normalized (CRLF to LF, each line's trailing whitespace trimmed, leading and trailing blank lines dropped) before hashing.

protected_apparatus.description: The files that produce this plan's number (FR-024): the measurement harness, the labels, corpus, or answer key, the file that selects the population, and the checker configuration. Each entry is a repository-relative path or glob; every entry must resolve to at least one real file, and each file it names is digested when a measurement collection is written -- Quoin's intake refuses a collection whose protected entry names no file. Part of the measurement definition: adding, removing, or changing an entry requires a new `definition_version`, and so does editing a protected file, which Quoin detects by its digest. Optional.

negative_controls.description: Gaming scenarios this plan's measurement must catch (FR-024), each a closed `kind` plus a `description` of how the measurement catches it. Required, with at least one entry, when `stage` is `gate`; optional otherwise.

relationships.description: Structural links to other spec artifacts. When a pass/fail decision genuinely depends on more than one metric succeeding together (a composite/AND gate), that composition MUST be expressed here as one `references` entry per constituent metric's MeasurementPlan -- never as a fabricated single `metric` id, and never only as prose. Do not add a separate constituent-metrics field for this; `references` is the one spelling of the edge.

apparatus_path.description: A repository-relative file path or glob (FR-024). Segments are separated by `/`. A segment is either exactly `**`, matching zero or more whole directories, or a name in which each `*` matches zero or more characters other than `/`; every other character is literal. Refused: an empty entry, a leading `/`, an empty segment (`//` or a trailing `/`), a `.` or `..` segment, `**` inside a longer segment, and the characters `\`, `?`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, `:` and control characters.

kind.description: `suppressed-observation`: an unfavourable item or run is left out of the collected population. `gain-within-noise`: an improvement smaller than the plan's stated uncertainty is claimed as a gain. `stale-evidence`: a result collected against an earlier subject version or apparatus is presented as current. `apparatus-edit`: a protected-apparatus file is edited alongside the change it grades. `selective-reporting`: only a favourable run or variant is reported out of several tried.

description.description: How this plan's measurement catches the scenario.

objective.description: Which way this plan's metric is supposed to move (FR-020). When a `statistical_design.decision_rule` is also present, its comparator agrees with `direction` (FR-021): `higher` takes `gt` or `ge`, `lower` takes `lt` or `le`, `zero` takes `eq` or `le` against threshold 0, and `target` takes any comparator. Part of the measurement definition: adding, removing, or changing it requires a new `definition_version`, so results under the old and new objective are never compared as one series. Optional.

direction.description: `higher`: a larger value is better. `lower`: a smaller value is better. `zero`: the metric is expected to be exactly zero; any non-zero value is a deviation. `target`: the metric is expected to reach `bound`, which is then required.

bound.description: The goal the metric should reach; informational, never evaluated. Only `statistical_design.decision_rule` is evaluated (FR-021). Required when `direction` is `target`; optional otherwise.

type.description: `measures`: this plan measures the target directly (e.g. the AssuranceProfile it informs). `references`: this plan points at a related artifact without measuring it, including -- for a composite/gate-stage decision -- each constituent metric's MeasurementPlan that the decision composes.

minimum_population.description: The smallest population size below which a result must not be trusted -- e.g. refuses the 'decided from two examples' failure mode. Optional; when set, a result collected against a smaller population is invalid and must be refused or flagged, not silently accepted.

repetitions.description: How many repeat runs are required before a result counts. The estimator is computed over every repetition together and decision_rule is applied once to that estimate. For a gate-stage plan, 'passes 3 of 5 tries' is therefore expressed as repetitions: 5, a metric that is the proportion of passing tries, estimator: proportion, and decision_rule { comparator: ge, threshold: 0.6 } -- it is not a separate field, so do not add a parallel required_repeats here or in decision_rule.

estimator.description: How the plan's metric is computed from the collected population (FR-021). `proportion`: matching items divided by examined items, in [0, 1]. `count`: the number of matching items. `mean`: the arithmetic mean of per-item or per-repetition values, including a weighted mean whose weights the plan's body states. `eq` against a `mean` or `ratio` estimate is exact floating-point equality. `median`: the middle per-item value. `ratio`: one total divided by another, unbounded (e.g. cost per confirmed finding).

decision_rule.description: The mechanical rule a checker applies to the plan's `metric` (FR-021): it holds when `estimate <comparator> reference`, where the estimate is computed under `estimator` over all `repetitions` and the reference is either `threshold` or the `baseline` value moved by `margin`. The rule is the only part of a MeasurementPlan that is evaluated; `objective.bound` is informational. It is part of the measurement definition: changing it requires a new `definition_version`, so a rule edited after results were seen starts a new series that is never compared with the old one. When `minimum_population` is set, a result over a smaller population is refused before the rule is evaluated. The rule does not restate `metric`, `repetitions`, or `minimum_population`.

comparator.description: `gt`: estimate > reference. `ge`: estimate >= reference. `lt`: estimate < reference. `le`: estimate <= reference. `eq`: estimate == reference, exact floating-point equality (e.g. a count gated at exactly zero). None of them holds when either side is NaN.

threshold.description: A fixed reference value stated in the plan. Exactly one of `threshold` and `baseline` is present. JSON Schema has no finiteness keyword, so a YAML `.inf` or `.nan` threshold passes this schema; the Rust `DecisionRule` refuses it.

baseline.description: A reference value computed at evaluation time, never written into the plan. `constant-predictor`: the agreement rate of the highest-scoring constant answer in each answer family, combined as the size-weighted mean over families (total best-constant agreements over total items), computed from the corpus (see the MeasurementPlan skeleton's worked example); allowed only with `estimator: proportion`. `prior-collection`: the plan's metric in the collection this result is compared against under the same definition_version (a branch comparison's base, or a trend's previous point). `best-seen`: over every accepted collection of the plan's metric under the same definition_version -- one the measurement intake admitted rather than refused -- the maximum value when `comparator` is `gt` or `ge`, and the minimum when it is `lt` or `le`; the value a ratchet refuses to regress past. `eq` against `best-seen` is refused. Exactly one of `threshold` and `baseline` is present.

margin.description: How far the result must improve on the baseline, in the metric's own units, signed in the direction of improvement: positive means the estimate must beat the baseline by at least this much, negative allows a regression of up to this much. reference = baseline value + margin for `gt` and `ge`, and baseline value - margin for `lt` and `le`. Allowed only with `baseline` and never with `eq`; absent means 0.
